classification: Public blank forms retrieved, not completed or submitted

paragraphs: Texas  Responsible  AI Governance Vendor Compliance Questionnaire ( TRAIGA -Aligned, Model Card Enhanced)
Section 1: Vendor & AI System Overview
Identify each AI system you  propose to  provide, including purpose, functionality, deployment environment, and intended end-users.
Confirm whether the system (s)   are  developed, deployed, or used in Texas or by Texas residents.
Provide version history and update/change logs for each AI system.
Section 2: Data  Management,  Security,  Privacy & Biometric Protections
How is data collected, stored and protected?
Does your system have data anonymization or encryption technology?
What cybersecurity measures are in place to protect the AI system?
Does the AI system capture, process, or store biometric data?
If yes, provide documentation of informed consent procedures, retention schedules, and secure deletion processes (Sec. 503.001 & Sec. 552.054).
Provide full data protection assessment reports, including compliance with Chapters 541 (Consumer Data Protection) and 521 (Unauthorized Use of Identifying Information).
Describe breach notification protocols and provide historical compliance evidence  as applicable .
Section 3: Prohibited Uses & Risk Mitigation
Confirm the system is not designed to:
Discriminate against protected classes (Sec. 552.056).
Manipulate behavior to incite self-harm or criminal activity (Sec. 552.052).
Conduct social scoring or assign social scores (Sec. 552.053).
Infringe constitutional rights (Sec. 552.055).
What procedures are in place to detect and mitigate bias in the system?  Describe  the remediation process when bias and or data drift is discovered.
Are fairness audits conducted regularly?
Section 4: Transparency, Model Cards, & Consumer Disclosures
Provide a model card for each AI system containing:
System purpose, intended use, and deployment scope.
Training data sources, description, and known limitations.
Performance metrics, accuracy, error rates, and failure modes.
Known  biases and mitigation measures.
Version history and updates.
Contact information for questions or complaints.
Describe how end-users are informed of AI interactions, including placement, timing, and language of disclosures.
Confirm disclosures are clear, conspicuous, and free from manipulative design (dark patterns).
Provide examples of notifications, disclaimers, and public-facing transparency materials.
Section 5: Regulatory & Oversight Compliance

Document participation in Texas AI regulatory sandbox (if applicable) ,  DIR approvals , and p rovide records of cooperation with oversight audits, reporting obligations, and Artificial      Intelligence Council inquiries.
Note any specific AI certifications and provide information outlining how your organization stays updated with evolving AI regulations.
Section 6 :  Ethical  Governance
Does your organization follow any ethical AI frameworks?
Is there an internal ethics committee overseeing AI projects?
Section  7 : Documentation Checklist (Vendor Submission)
AI system functional specifications and architecture diagrams.
Model card(s)  including  all items listed above.
Data privacy/security policies, including encryption, retention, and deletion procedures.
Bias and fairness testing results, validation datasets, and mitigation actions.
Biometric consent forms and deletion logs.
Sample user notifications, disclaimers, and public-facing transparency materials.
Regulatory approvals, sandbox participation documents, and audit reports.
Section 1:  Security Governance & Organizational Oversight
Does your organization engage executive oversight for cybersecurity? If yes, describe your organization's information security governance structure.
Does your organization have a designated Information Security Officer? If not, who has primary responsibility for your organization's information security program?
Does your organization have defined, documented information security standards, policies, and supporting procedures? If yes, identify the foundational framework (NIST, ISO, et.  al .) in use.
Does your organization engage in information security audits and/or risk assessments? If yes, how often are they performed? Are these engagements performed in-house or outsourced to third parties?
Does your organization outsource - in whole or in part - cybersecurity functions to third party service providers? If yes, identify the outsourced functions and those performed in-house.
Section 2:  Product, Service  & Regulatory Classification

Is your proposed product or service  considered  a medical device subject to regulation by the Food and Drug Administration? If yes, provide a Manufacturer Disclosure Statement for Medical Device Security (MDS2) for each proposed product/service.

Does your proposed product or service require access and use of JPS confidential data? If yes, please identify the necessary data elements. "Confidential data" refers to Protected Health Information (HIPAA), Cardholder Data (PCI), or other data intended for restricted access or use.
Please describe the purpose of the data request and how the data will be used.
Please explain why the requested data elements are necessary to accomplish the stated business purpose.
Does your product or service have the capability to generate an audit trail of access and use? If yes, please describe this feature.
Section 3:  Application Security & Software Development
Is a formal software development process in place that includes application security requirements?
Are security reviews and regression testing performed on application source code?
Is the proposed product or service subject to industry certifications? If yes, please describe. If your product or service is subject to SOC-II requirements, please provide your most recent report.
Are non-production environments used for development and testing, prior to deployment in production?

Does your organization have a formal change management process for testing and approving production environment changes? If yes, provide describe the process for review, approval, implementation, and monitoring these changes.
Section 4:  Identify & Access Management
Does your organization require all users to have unique user accounts on systems that store, access, and or transmit customer data?
Are user accounts assigned based on the principle of "least privilege"?
Does your organization enforce strong password policies? If yes, please describe your current password controls.
Does your organization utilize  roles -based security when provisioning user accounts? If yes, please describe how roles are defined, monitored, and revised to meet organizational needs.

Does your organization perform account user access reviews? If yes, how often are these reviews performed? Describe the user access review process including account selection, issue documentation, and corrective actions.
Is cybersecurity training provided to your workforce? If yes, how often is this training provided? How is training content selected, developed, and delivered?
Is the effectiveness of cybersecurity training evaluated? If so, please describe the evaluation process.
Is two-factor authentication implemented for environments containing customer data? If yes, what authentication products are used by your organization?
Does your organization require authentication for remote access to server environments?
Does your organization verify deactivation of login credentials upon end of employment or contract service? If yes, describe the process.
Will vendor personnel or external users have access to JPS data? If yes, identify the number and type of users requiring access.
Section 5:  Third-Party Services & Hosting Environment

Will your organization utilize third parties to provide - in whole or in part - the proposed product or service? If yes, describe how  third party  staff are vetted, provisioned upon start of contract service, and de-provisioned upon end of contract service.
Will data be shared with any third parties, vendors, contractors, consultants, or external entities? If yes, please identify all parties and describe the purpose of sharing.
Does your organization staff its data centers? If not, identify your data center service provider. Identify the number and location of your data centers.
Are any of your organizations' data centers located outside of the United States? If yes, please identify the locations of these "offshore" data centers.

If offshore data centers are in use, are they staffed by your  organizations'  workforce or outsourced to  third-parties ? If outsourced, please confirm that staff agreements cover appropriate data confidentiality requirements.
Is your  organizations'  customer data stored in a hosted "cloud" environment? If yes, identify your cloud service provider.
Section 6:   Vulnerability Management & Security Testing
Are periodic vulnerability scans performed on information technology systems, networks and supporting security systems?

Does your organization conduct penetration testing of internal and external data environments? If yes, is the testing performed in-house or outsourced to third parties? How often is penetration testing performed?

Has your organization experienced a data breach  within in  the past two years? If yes, please describe the breach and corrective measures implemented. Was the breach required to be reported to one or more regulatory authorities?
Section  7 :  Business Continuity, Incident Response & Data Lif ecycle Management
Does your organization maintain disaster recovery and/or business continuity plans? If yes, how often are the plans  tested  and updated? What  manner  of testing is used?
Does your organization maintain a cybersecurity incident response plan? If yes, how often is the plan  tested  and updated? What  manner  of testing is used?
Will the requested data be retained, archived, accumulated longitudinally, or stored beyond the immediate operational use case? If yes, describe the retention and accumulation practices.
Upon termination of services or completion of the business need, how will JPS data be returned, destroyed, or otherwise disposed of?
